questions.q: Arrange in increasing heat of hydrogenation: but-1-ene (I), cis-but-2-ene (II), trans-but-2-ene (III), 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene (IV).
questions.explain: The more stable alkene releases less heat: tetrasubstituted > trans-disubstituted > cis-disubstituted > monosubstituted, so IV releases least and I most.

questions.q: Which diene is the most stable?
questions.explain: Conjugated dienes are stabilised by delocalisation of π electrons over four carbons, so the order is conjugated > isolated > cumulated.

questions.q: The correct increasing order of heat of hydrogenation is:
questions.explain: Benzene releases about 206 kJ/mol, less than cyclohexa-1,3-diene (about 230) despite having more π bonds, because of about 150 kJ/mol aromatic stabilisation; cyclohexene releases about 118.

questions.q: Which statement about relative stability is correct?
options: Heats of combustion of cyclopropene and methylenecyclopropane can be compared directly to rank their stability
Methylenecyclopropane is more stable than 1-methylcyclopropene, but 1-methylcyclohexene is more stable than methylenecyclohexane
questions.explain: In three-membered rings an endocyclic C=C adds severe strain, so the exo isomer wins; in six-membered rings strain is not the issue and the more substituted endocyclic alkene wins. Cyclopropene and methylenecyclopropane are not isomers, so their heats of combustion cannot be compared.
